name: Anthropic AI for Science Program (API credits)
amount: Up to USD 20,000 in Claude API credits
eligibility: Researchers at academic or non-profit research institutions working on high-impact scientific topics; Computer Science explicitly listed (biology/life sciences is a particular focus).
eligibility_note: No nationality restriction on the program page; Anthropic's supported-countries list includes Pakistan.
deadline: Rolling (selections on first Monday of each month)
how_to_apply_tip: Frame the work as AI-for-science (e.g. AI applied to health, climate or materials) rather than pure ML; group collaborators under one organisation ID application. Unsuccessful applicants get no reply.

name: Cohere Labs Catalyst Grants
amount: Cohere API credits (amount not published; more can be requested)
eligibility: Academic partners and civic/public-impact organisations doing public-benefit or open-science research (focus: education, healthcare, climate, sustainability).
eligibility_note: Official page lists no geographic limits and highlights grantees from many countries.
how_to_apply_tip: Strong fit for multilingual/Urdu NLP or low-resource language projects; emphasise open-science outputs and public benefit.

name: Gemini Academic Program (Gemini API credits for research)
amount: Gemini API credits and higher rate limits (amount at Google's discretion)
eligibility: Qualified academic researchers (faculty, staff, PhD students) affiliated with an academic institution or research organisation; priority areas: evaluations/benchmarks, scientific discovery, embodied AI/robotics, emergent capabilities, multimodal understanding.
eligibility_note: Open to researchers in Gemini API supported countries; Google's available-regions page lists Pakistan.
how_to_apply_tip: Frame the project as an evaluation/benchmark or multimodal study and give a concrete token-usage estimate; postdocs should apply as institutional research staff.

name: Google Cloud Research Credits
amount: Up to USD 5,000 for faculty/postdocs (secondary sources); up to USD 1,000/year for PhD students (official)
eligibility: Faculty, PhD students and postdoctoral researchers at accredited higher-education or non-profit research institutions in eligible countries.
eligibility_note: Google's official eligibility FAQ lists eligible countries and Pakistan is on the list; postdocs explicitly eligible.
how_to_apply_tip: Create a Google Cloud billing account first and attach a pricing-calculator cost estimate to the short proposal; activate credits within 60 days of project start.

name: Hugging Face Community GPU Grants (Spaces)
amount: Free GPU hardware upgrade for a Hugging Face Space (e.g. T4/A10G/A100 class)
eligibility: Anyone with an innovative, public Hugging Face Space/demo.
eligibility_note: Official docs set no nationality or institutional requirement.
how_to_apply_tip: Request from your Space's Settings (hardware section); best for showcasing a paper's model as a live demo.

name: Lambda Research Grant
amount: Up to USD 5,000 in Lambda Cloud credits
eligibility: 'Qualifying researchers' (criteria not published on the page).
eligibility_note: No country rule published; Lambda Cloud account availability from Pakistan should be confirmed at sign-up.
how_to_apply_tip: Short Typeform application – link a recent paper or GitHub repo showing GPU-heavy work.

name: Modal for Academics (research credits)
amount: Up to USD 10,000 in Modal credits
eligibility_note: No country rule stated on the official page; currently a sign-up/interest form for grant rounds.
deadline: Rolling (sign up to be notified of grant rounds)
how_to_apply_tip: Register on the academics page to be notified; Modal suits serverless GPU inference/batch jobs written in Python.

name: Nebius Research Grants (Research Credits Program)
amount: GPU cloud credits + Token Factory tokens + Tavily credits (amount set per proposal)
eligibility: Postgraduate students, PhD students, postdoctoral researchers and faculty at accredited academic institutions or non-profit research organisations; non-commercial intent required.
eligibility_note: Official page states no country restrictions; postdocs explicitly eligible.
deadline: Rolling (monthly cycles; submit by last day of a month)
how_to_apply_tip: Include a transparent GPU-hour utilisation plan; if not contacted by end of the following month, revise and resubmit.

name: OpenAI Researcher Access Program
amount: Up to USD 1,000 in OpenAI API credits
eligibility: Researchers at legitimate research institutions; proposals reviewed for research relevance (companies/startups not eligible).
eligibility_note: No nationality rule found; OpenAI API supported-countries list includes Pakistan, so credits are usable.
how_to_apply_tip: Apply from the account tied to your institution – credits cannot be moved to another account or institution later.

name: TPU Research Cloud (TRC)
amount: Free access to Cloud TPUs (cluster of 1,000+ TPU devices); other GCP costs (VMs, storage) not covered
eligibility: Researchers worldwide; must share TRC-supported research publicly (papers/open source) and give feedback to Google.
eligibility_note: Official FAQ: 'Anyone can express interest'; no country restrictions stated (Google Cloud account required, which is available in Pakistan).
how_to_apply_tip: Fill the short 'Express interest' form; have JAX/PyTorch-XLA code ready because the free quota clock starts once invited – pair with Google Cloud Research Credits to cover VM/storage costs.

name: Weights & Biases Academic (free research license)
amount: Free W&B platform access for academic research (in-kind)
eligibility_note: Official page: 'Free for students, educators, and academic researchers. Always.' – no country restriction mentioned.
how_to_apply_tip: Sign up with your university email to get the academic tier; useful as in-kind support to list in grant budgets.

name: Yotta Labs Academic Research Support Program
amount: USD 1,000 in GPU compute credits + discounted compute for 6 months
eligibility: Faculty, graduate and postdoctoral researchers at accredited academic/non-profit institutions, and independent non-commercial researchers.
eligibility_note: Official page specifies no country restrictions; postdocs explicitly eligible. Page says offer is 'valid for a limited time only'.
deadline: Rolling (limited-time offer, end date not stated)
how_to_apply_tip: Apply soon given the limited-time wording; describe feasibility and a transparent resource plan.

name: SIGCHI Gary Marsden Travel Awards
amount: Varies with available funds (registration code + reimbursement of travel costs)
duration: One-off per conference (physical travel support max once every 3 years)
eligibility: Students, early-career researchers (up to 5 years post-graduation), or those facing financial hardship / lacking institutional support; must be SIGCHI member when applying; attending SIGCHI-sponsored/in-cooperation conferences
eligibility_note: No nationality restriction stated; priority to financial need and benefit to applicant, which favours researchers from low-income countries.
how_to_apply_tip: Seven cycles a year (9th of Jan, Feb, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov); apply to a cycle more than one month before the conference, and buy SIGCHI membership (cheap developing-country rate) before submitting on Submittable.

name: Heidelberg Laureate Forum - Young Researchers (14th HLF, 2027)
amount: Hotel (single room), meals and airport shuttles covered for the HLF week (11-18 Sep 2027); separate HLFF travel grant may reimburse travel and visa costs if home institution/agency will not
eligibility: Undergraduates, PhD students and postdocs in mathematics or computer science; postdocs must have PhD within the last 5 years (+1 year per child)
eligibility_note: Official FAQ lists no nationality restriction; eligibility depends only on field and academic level. Visa invitation letter provided.
how_to_apply_tip: Application window opens 11 Nov 2026; for the travel grant you must upload a rejection letter from your institution/HEC showing other funding was sought, so request that early.

name: HEC Research Travel Grant (paper presentation at international conferences)
amount: International travel: airfare as per Government rules + registration fee up to USD 500 (reimbursed after the event)
duration: One-off per trip (max one grant per person per financial year)
eligibility: Principal (first/corresponding) author presenting a peer-reviewed, archived paper; faculty members (not visiting faculty) or MS/MPhil/PhD scholars of public-sector HEIs and eligible private universities
eligibility_note: National programme for Pakistani university faculty and scholars. Postdocs are not named explicitly; a postdoc holding a faculty/research appointment at a Pakistani HEI should confirm with their ORIC. Max 20 grants per university per financial year.
how_to_apply_tip: Apply on research.hec.gov.pk via your university's ORIC with the acceptance letter stating mode of presentation; get NOCs from all co-authors and apply well before travel.
